title: Largest Element in an Array
statement: You are given n integers. Print the largest of them.

mistakes.hint1: What would your answer be if every number in the array were negative?
mistakes.hint2: Starting the maximum at 0 only works when some element is at least 0.
mistakes.hint3: What could you start it with so it works for any array? Think about the very first element.
mistakes.hint4: Try initializing your maximum variable with array[0] or INT_MIN.

mistakes.hint1: The largest number is at the last position in T3. Does your loop examine that position?
mistakes.hint2: For n numbers, valid indexes range from 0 to n-1. Check where your loop stops.
mistakes.hint3: Trace your loop with n = 4. If it stops at index 2, it misses the value 9 at index 3.
mistakes.hint4: Make sure your loop visits the last valid index. For a zero-based array, a common condition is i < n.

mistakes.hint1: Re-read the condition that decides when your stored maximum is replaced.
mistakes.hint2: Run your code by hand on 3, 1, 4. Is it storing the biggest value seen so far?
mistakes.hint3: Check whether you accidentally wrote logic to find the minimum instead of the maximum.
mistakes.hint4: Update the maximum only when the current element is greater than the current maximum.

mistakes.hint1: Are you printing the largest number, or its position?
mistakes.hint2: The problem asks for the value itself, not the index where it was found.
mistakes.hint3: For the array 9, 2, 3, check whether your output is 9 or 0.
mistakes.hint4: Print the actual maximum value, such as max_val, rather than the index.
